method: Reuse G1 gsplat packed tile extraction; port teacher (M-Gaussian alpha composite) and student (rank-R CGT mixture) to torch GPU; CUDA-event timing, warmup+median. Two regimes: per-tile (256px, launch-bound) and intrinsic (65536px single call, launch-free math ratio). Params created once; no H2D in timing loops.
pending_reason: GPUs 5/6/7 were idle at start but became occupied by other users mid-run; respecting the idle-only constraint, did not run on occupied GPUs.

findings.headline: Raw-math per-component advantage is REAL and LARGER than the G1/G2 assumed gamma=2-4: measured intrinsic gamma = 6.3x (M_med=60) to 10.5x (M_med=267), growing with M (teacher cost ~ M, student cost ~ R fixed). BUT at 256px/tile granularity the GPU is launch/dispatch-bound, so operational per-tile gamma is only ~1.35 and end-to-end S ~ 1.18-1.20x. The 6-10x math headroom is locked behind per-tile launch overhead (~11% floor + many small kernels).
findings.implication_for_G4: A fused/batched CGT CUDA kernel that amortizes launch across many tiles/components is the critical path to realize the 6-10x math headroom. Measured h (~11%) is BELOW the G2 budget (26.6%), so overhead alone does not kill 3x; the binding constraint is per-tile launch granularity, which a fused kernel (G4) must remove.
findings.contrast_with_G1_G2: G1/G2 Amdahl bound used ASSUMED gamma=2-4 (zero-overhead). Measured gamma is 6-10x (better), so the zero-overhead bound was pessimistic on gamma; but the zero-overhead assumption ignored launch overhead, which is the real killer. Net: operational S ~1.2x << the 15-44x zero-overhead bound.
